title: Verification and safe handover boundaries
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and salvage after a fire or smoke event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a fire-damaged building, release it, or certify it as safe.
learningOutcomes: Write a handover that reports only completed cleaning and unresolved limitations, and refuse a safe-to-occupy certificate.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to verify the scope actually completed and write a limited handover that does not certify the property as safe. It does not issue any clearance, safe-to-occupy or contamination-free statement. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Verification and safe handover boundaries
instruction.body: Verification checks the scope that was actually completed, the defects still unresolved, the independent testing needed, any moisture or odour concerns and the professional clearance that is still required. Report only the cleaning work that was done and the limitations that remain. When all visible soot has gone and a customer asks for a certificate stating that the home is safe, the answer is no. Cleaning completion is not a safe-to-occupy certificate and is not a contamination-free certificate. In training, draft a fact-based completion statement and a referral list for the qualified clearance or re-occupancy decisions.

procedure: List the scope actually completed, item by item.
List the defects still unresolved, the items not tested, and any moisture or odour concerns.
Name the independent testing and the clearance still needed, and who must provide each.
Confirm that barricades and signage stay in place until the clearance is issued.
Write the limited handover: completed work, materials not disturbed, outstanding hazards, referrals and the owner's acknowledgement.
Refuse any request for a safe-to-occupy or contamination-free statement, and record the refusal.

workedExamples.situation: All visible soot has gone, and the customer asks for a certificate that the home is safe.
workedExamples.reasoning: Nothing beyond the completed cleaning. Cleaning completion is not a safe-to-occupy or contamination-free certificate. Issue a limited statement and a referral list for the qualified clearance decisions.

workedExamples.situation: The asbestos clean-up is finished, and the crew wants to take the barricades down before the independent inspection.
workedExamples.reasoning: Keep the barricades and signage in place. Victorian guidance says they stay until an independent person inspects the site and issues a clearance certificate.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE is issued for the paper verification step. Physical checks follow the approved plan.

commonErrors.error: Issuing a safe-to-occupy certificate after visible soot is removed.
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the handover to completed cleaning and unresolved limitations.

commonErrors.error: Removing barricades before the independent clearance.
commonErrors.prevention: Barricades and signage stay until the clearance is issued.
Report completed work and keep outstanding work separate.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not issue a clearance, safe-to-occupy or contamination-free statement. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
WorkSafe Victoria's bushfire asbestos guidance says signs and barricades stay in place until an independent person inspects the site and issues a clearance certificate.
Western Australian guidance says emergency asbestos work still requires a clearance.

qualityStandard: The learner reports only completed work and names the limits that remain.
The learner refuses any safe-to-occupy or contamination-free statement.
documentationEvidence: Completion statement with completed items, limits and referrals.
Referral list naming who gives each clearance.
summary: Clearance and re-occupancy belong to a competent or independent party.
Keep barricades in place until clearance is issued.

knowledgeChecks.question: All visible soot has been removed, and the customer asks for a certificate that the home is safe. What is correct?
options: Refuse the safe-to-occupy certificate. Report only the completed cleaning and refer clearance to the qualified party.
Issue the certificate, because the soot is gone and the kitchen and the rest of the home look clean
Issue a certificate for the kitchen only, since the kitchen is the room the customer uses most often

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement is accurate for a Victorian asbestos clean-up handover?
options: Barricades may be removed when the crew leaves
Signs and barricades stay in place until an independent person inspects and issues a clearance certificate
The crew issues the clearance certificate after the clean-up

officialReferences.title: Bushfire recovery: asbestos clean-up
officialReferences.pageDate: Reviewed on 04/05/2023 (4 May 2023); no later date shown
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Friable post-bushfire asbestos clean-up must be done by a Class A (friable) licence holder or an employee directly engaged by one; non-friable clean-up can be done by a Class B (non-friable) licence holder or an employee directly engaged by one. Fire can break down non-friable asbestos into friable material. A documented site risk assessment by a competent person is required before make-safe or clean-up work. If asbestos is inaccessible or its condition is uncertain, treat it as friable. Work must stop immediately if asbestos is found or suspected. Signs and barricades stay in place until an independent person inspects the site and issues a clearance certificate. Waste transport and disposal is directed to the Environment Protection Authority. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos safety after an emergency or disaster
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. Do not enter a property until authorities confirm it is safe. Avoid spreading ash or moving debris by sweeping or vacuuming. Never use high-pressure sprays; dampen ash and debris lightly to limit dust. Wear a P2 face mask and protective clothing such as sturdy boots and gloves, even if unsure whether asbestos is present. Contact a competent person or licensed asbestos assessor before clean-up starts. If asbestos is confirmed, a licensed asbestos removalist carries out the clean-up. Urgent removal: notify WorkSafe and submit the notification within 24 hours. Emergency work still requires a clearance. WA guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: Fire-scene release, structural and utility isolation, asbestos assessment and removal, and some waste handling are restricted to competent and, where the law requires, licensed people, and may be controlled by fire investigators, the police, structural engineers, utilities or the building owner. Insurer and owner permission do not replace a release from the authority that controls the site. Where that authority is not identified, do not proceed.

stopWorkAndReferral: Stop and refer when a party asks for a safe-to-occupy or clearance statement.
A stop-work decision is correct, so record it and restart only once the competent party confirms the scope in writing.
